title: Joyal weak equivalences tested by whole functor quasicategories
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and coherent functor equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Joyal model structure and ordinary homotopy category $h$ from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $u:A\to B$ be a map of small simplicial sets. For every quasicategory $C$, both $\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)$ are quasicategories. The following three conditions are equivalent: (i) $u$ is a weak equivalence of the Joyal model structure; (ii) for every quasicategory $C$ in any sufficiently large universe, precomposition $u^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ is a coherent functor equivalence (it admits a quasi-inverse with coherent natural equivalences of both composites with the identities); (iii) for every such $C$, the induced ordinary functor $h(u^*):h\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories. The equivalence in (ii) is required for the specified precomposition map, retaining all transformations and higher simplices.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026 revision, Theorem 3.6.8 (i)-(iii), printed pp.115-116; Corollary 3.6.4 and Remark 3.6.5 identify internal Homs and coherent functor equivalences. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: First fix a universe containing the simplicial sets in use. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,C)=\Delta^0$ is an isofibration between quasicategories for every quasicategory $C$ and small $K$: take the degreewise injective inclusion $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ in its particular assertion. Thus $C^K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)$ is a quasicategory, including when $K$ or $C$ is empty. In particular put $D=C^B$, $E=C^A$ and $p=u^*:D\to E$.

source.place: Internal-Hom fibrancy; compare Corollary 3.6.7. Agent-written specialization of the cited statement.

proof.text: Assume (iii), and fix a test quasicategory $C$. For every small simplicial set $K$ there are simplicial isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C^B)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(B,C^K)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C^A)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(A,C^K)$. Explicitly an $n$-simplex is a map $K\times B\times\Delta^n\to C$, respectively $K\times A\times\Delta^n\to C$; interchanging the first two factors gives the isomorphisms and commutes with all simplicial operators. Under these isomorphisms postcomposition by $p$ is restriction along $u$ into $C^K$. Step 1 makes $C^K$ an allowed test in (iii). Consequently $F_K=h\operatorname{Fun}(K,p):h\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories for every $K$, including $K=E,D$.

source.place: Agent-written currying calculation for Theorem 3.6.8(iii) implies (ii); the statement of the model-structure node specifies h.

proof.text: Use essential surjectivity of $F_E$ to choose a vertex $s:E\to D$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:ps\cong1_E$ in $h\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)$. Precomposing $\alpha$ with $p$ gives $\alpha p:psp\cong p$ in $h\operatorname{Fun}(D,E)$. Fullness of $F_D$ lifts $\alpha p$ and its inverse to arrows $\beta:sp\to1_D$ and $\gamma:1_D\to sp$ in $h\operatorname{Fun}(D,D)$. Their composites map to identities, so faithfulness gives $\gamma\beta=1_{sp}$ and $\beta\gamma=1_{1_D}$. Thus $sp\cong1_D$. Both functor simplicial sets here are quasicategories by Step 1. Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval] to their pairs of isomorphic vertices. It gives maps $J\to\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)$ and $J\to\operatorname{Fun}(D,D)$ with endpoints $(ps,1_E)$ and $(sp,1_D)$. In $J$, the arrows $0\to1$ and $1\to0$ and the two triangles with vertex lists $(0,1,0)$ and $(1,0,1)$ witness both inverse equations. Their images therefore give equivalence edges with the same endpoints. These are exactly the coherent natural equivalences required by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The simplicial map $s$ is a quasi-inverse of the actual $p=u^*$, proving (ii).

source.place: Agent-written explicit inverse construction using the invertible interval; compare Remark 3.6.5 and Theorem 3.6.8. No cartesian-model or Brown lemma is used.

proof.text: Conversely assume (ii) and write $s:E\to D$ for a coherent quasi-inverse of $p$. To see directly that a coherent equivalence $H:f\to g$ induces a natural isomorphism $hf\cong hg$, evaluate its edge and inverse edge at each vertex $x$. Evaluating their two inverse triangles gives mutually inverse arrows $H_x$ in $h$ of the target. For each edge $a:x\to y$ of the source, $H$ restricts to a map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ into the target. The two triangular faces give $[g(a)][H_x]=[H_y][f(a)]$. This proves naturality on edge generators; composition and the triangle relations defining $h$ extend it to every arrow. Apply this calculation to the two equivalences $sp\simeq1_D$ and $ps\simeq1_E$. Their components and naturality make $hs$ a quasi-inverse to $hp$, proving (iii).

source.place: Agent-written generators-and-triangles calculation for Theorem 3.6.8(ii) implies (iii).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], a weak equivalence is exactly a categorical equivalence, and its definition is the equivalence of $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ for every test quasicategory $C$. Therefore (i) and (iii) are identical conditions. Steps 2--4 identify (iii) with (ii), completing all implications. All constructions take place in a universe containing $A,B,C$ and its internal Homs; that universe is closed under the products and sets of maps used in currying. Hence $D,E,C^D,C^E$ are legitimate small tests there. Repeat for every sufficiently large testing universe. The weak-equivalence testing condition in the model-structure statement already uses this convention, so the quantifiers agree and the equivalence data is for the specified restriction map in every such universe.

source.place: Agent-written assembly and universe check for Theorem 3.6.8(i)--(iii).

lean.statement: theorem joyal_functor_equivalence_test (M : HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory SSet.{u}) (hJoyal : ∀ {X Y : SSet.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y), M.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences g ↔ ∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map g)).app C)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) {A B : SSet.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B) : (∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → Quasicategory ((ihom (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.obj A)).obj C) ∧ Quasicategory ((ihom (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.obj B)).obj C)) ∧ List.TFAE [ M.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences f, ∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → Enhanced.IsFunctorEquivalence ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map f)).app C), ∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map f)).app C)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence]
